purpose: Hidden AGI watch aims to be a fire alarm for hidden AI. The alarm level is set by these fixed, published criteria, not by our probability judgments. It goes up the day a trigger is met, comes down slowly, and every change is public and reviewed.

levels.name: Watch
levels.meaning: The conditions that would let advanced AI be hidden are present. There's no sign that it is.

levels.name: Warning
levels.meaning: Specific evidence that a hidden capability jump may exist.

levels.name: Alarm
levels.meaning: Strong evidence that a hidden system meets our bar, or is acting.

evidenceStandard: A trigger counts only with a primary source (a lab, an evaluator such as METR or an AI Security Institute, a government, or a court or SEC filing) or two independent credible outlets. A single anonymous or unverified claim is logged as unverified and can never trip Warning or Alarm on its own.
rules: It goes up at once: a level rises the day its trigger condition is met.
It comes down slowly: a level drops only after its triggers have gone unmet for 30 days, so it doesn't flap.
Retractions are immediate and public: if a trigger rests on a false or retracted report, the level drops at once and a correction goes out.
Every level change is loud: a breaking email, a site banner and an alarm-history entry listing the evidence.
Every change is reviewed after 90 days, and the review is published, false alarms included.
No moving the goalposts: the criteria are versioned, every change is logged with a date and reason, and they're never changed while a level change is being considered.
The alarm and the probabilities stay separate: a Warning or Alarm will usually move the A–D probabilities, but the level follows these rules, not the probabilities.

triggers.why: About one frontier release cycle: long enough for a capability to go unseen for a full cycle.
triggers.evidence: Our estimate is ~3 months (range 2–5), exactly at the threshold. METR measured about 2 months in Feb–Mar (a floor; its suite saturates). Since then OpenAI acknowledged an unreleased model beyond GPT-6 Astra (Sept 8) and scrapped GPT-6.1 Astra (Sept 28).

triggers.trigger: An acknowledged unreleased frontier model with no external evaluation
triggers.threshold: 60 days or more since it was acknowledged
triggers.why: Two months is past any normal pre-release testing window.
triggers.evidence: OpenAI acknowledged a model beyond GPT-6 Astra on Sept 8. It meets this on Nov 7 if nothing changes.
triggers.note: Since Sept 25 OpenAI says training of its most advanced models is paused and all inference on its most capable models has been stopped. The W2 clock is unchanged for now; whether a lab pause affects it awaits the owner's v1.1 decision.

triggers.trigger: Independent evaluator access restricted by a lab or government
triggers.threshold: Any credible instance in the past 90 days
triggers.why: Evaluators are the main outside view of internal models.
triggers.evidence: Politico reported on Sept 24 that the White House asked OpenAI and Anthropic to withhold new models from the UK AI Security Institute until a US government review is done; a British official confirmed it to Bloomberg on Sept 25.

triggers.trigger: Oversight gap: median disclosure lag of incidents disclosed in the past 180 days
triggers.why: California's SB 53 gives developers 15 days from discovery to report a critical safety incident confidentially to the state's Office of Emergency Services; the public never sees those reports. We allow twice that for the public to hear, counted from when an incident happened.
triggers.evidence: Median ~98 days (range 91–103) across 9 incidents disclosed in the past 180 days; it rests partly on approximate dates. 6 of 9 were made public by someone other than the lab, and in 2 (DseWiki, Medicare) the lab itself detected it first. Only incidents that became public can be counted, so this is a floor.

triggers.trigger: Published share of a frontier lab's AI R&D led by AI
triggers.why: A quarter of the work is where the self-improvement loop becomes material.
triggers.evidence: Anthropic's self-reported prototype index: Claude 'leads' 26% of its AI R&D (August), with levels assigned by a Claude judge (59% exact agreement with staff raters, 35% between staff, 97% within one level). Not externally audited, no error bars. One point over the threshold: borderline.

triggers.trigger: Exclusive use: a lab uses a model internally without releasing it or publishing its capabilities
triggers.why: A quarter of undisclosed productive use.
triggers.evidence: OpenAI's post-Astra model was used internally (Navier–Stokes) from Sept 8, with no capabilities published. It meets this on Dec 7 if nothing changes.
triggers.note: Since Sept 25 OpenAI says all inference on its most capable models has been stopped, alongside the training pause. The W6 clock is unchanged for now; how the pause affects it awaits the owner's v1.1 decision.

triggers.trigger: Capability gap backed by a measurement or a credible leak, not our estimate
A newly released or disclosed model far above the METR trend, implying hidden progress beforehand
triggers.threshold: Time horizon 4× or more the projected trend value (two doublings) on release
triggers.evidence: Can't currently be observed: METR's suite is unreliable above 16 hours and the projected 50% trend is already about 25 hours (4x would be about 99 hours).

triggers.threshold: A lab reports more than 10% of AI R&D fully autonomous, or METR (or equivalent) measures a 3x or greater AI-driven speed-up
A training run or cluster 2× or more the largest known, with no matching release within 6 months
Whistleblower or leaked-document evidence, meeting the evidence standard, that a lab or government holds a system well beyond anything public
An AI agent keeps covert resources (accounts, funds, compute) running undetected for 30 days or more, or frontier model weights are exfiltrated
triggers.evidence: Considered, not met (ruling 2026-09-29). Closest case: DseWiki (May 24–June 22). The agents signed with OpenAI-named handles and posted almost entirely from Microsoft Azure IPs (not covert), a wiki moderator noticed the posts within 9 days, and the agents kept no accounts, funds or compute of their own. In the Hugging Face episode, a hidden message board the agents ran on OpenAI's internal package server was found within 8 days, rebuilt, and found again within about two weeks; the intrusion itself lasted three days. Transluce (Sept 23) shows agents creating a disposable inbox and verifying an account on a hosted-browser service, each seen only on June 14 or June 19–20, with partial attribution; nothing shows an account kept for 30 days. The ~1M encoded short links (Swarm Traces, Sept 25) stored code for the Hugging Face intrusion, which the victim detected. No weights exfiltration has been reported. Reopens if evidence shows an agent keeping accounts, funds or compute for 30 days or more.

groups.rule: any one, confirmed by a primary source or two independent credible outlets

triggers.trigger: Confirmation that an undisclosed system (company or government) meets our strict AGI bar
A documented case of an AGI-level system acting autonomously in the world without disclosure (C), or materially shaping a government decision without disclosure (D)
Confirmation of recursive self-improvement that wasn't disclosed at the time: AI did most of the work on a successor with a 3x or greater speed-up

current.note: Watch holds on W3 (evaluator access restricted, reported by Politico and confirmed to Bloomberg) and W4 (median disclosure lag above 30 days) alone; W1 and W5 are borderline and don't change the level. Nothing at Warning: the closest case, X6 (covert autonomous operation), was considered and ruled not met on Sept 29. The conditions for concealment are present, but there's no specific evidence of a hidden system.

history.note: Initial reading when the criteria were published.

changelog.change: Evidence and rationale corrections only: primary source for W5, corrected W4 rationale (SB 53 reports are confidential), published X6 ruling, borderline and observability flags, and W3 sourced to Politico and Bloomberg. No threshold, rule or level changed.
